_source: Ministry of Education / Curriculum Development Centre, Zambia. 'History Syllabus, Grade 10-12' (2013, published by CDC) — Grade 10, Part I: History of Southern Africa, Topics 10.1-10.5. Topic, sub-topic and Specific Outcome statements only; the 'Content' (Knowledge/Skills/Values) columns are omitted, consistent with the approach used for the other 2013 OBC subjects in this app. As with the other OBC syllabi processed, this document's printed outcome numbering codes drift (most sub-topic outcomes in 10.2 and 10.4 are all printed under one shared code prefix rather than incrementing), so outcomes were reconstructed positionally against each sub-topic heading rather than trusting the printed codes. Under 10.3, only 5 outcomes are printed for 6 named sub-topics; the outcome 'Describe the arrival of the European settlers at the Cape' clearly covers both 10.3.1 (arrival of the Dutch) and 10.3.2 (arrival of the British) together, so those two sub-topics are merged into one entry here rather than inventing a second outcome. This is distinct from the CBC_2023 History syllabus already in this app (history_form1.json, Form 1 only, Ordinary Level 2024 syllabus) — this file is the older 2013 Outcome-Based Curriculum's senior-secondary History syllabus. The syllabus organizes content by Grade only, not by Term, so all of Grade 10 is modeled as a single term here. UPDATE (2026-08-30): term-split and references added, sourced from a real, clean (no PII found) Ministry 'HISTORY COMMON SCHEMES OF WORK' covering all three terms for Grade 10-12 (Drive folder shared by the user 2026-08-30). The real document is far more granular (distinct weekly topics, e.g. separate weeks for the San/Khoikhoi/Bantu/Nguni/Great Trek/Mineral Revolution/Mfecane) than this file's existing coarser sub-topic grouping -- each existing sub-topic was assigned the real week where its core content is introduced in the source, grouping several real weeks under one sub-topic where they clearly belong together, rather than fragmenting the existing (already reliable) sub-topic structure to match the source 1:1. One genuine structural finding: the source places 'The Mfecane' in Term 2 even though its bundled siblings under '10.2 Indigenous Communities' are Term 1 content -- that topic is split across both Term objects rather than forced into one, reflecting what the source actually shows. References use the two authors cited on nearly every real row (G. Haantobolo; N.E. Davis) -- the introductory weeks' additional citations (Needham, Fagan, Dasgupta) apply to syllabus-overview/methodology content this file doesn't separately model.
